title: Blue marble - NASA Science
snippet: NASA's Visible Earth catalog entry for the Blue Marble image.
quote: Using a collection of satellite-based observations, scientists and visualizers stitched together months of observations of the land surface, oceans, sea ice, and clouds into a seamless, true-color mosaic of every square kilometer (0.4 square miles) of our planet.
stance_why: NASA itself describes the iconic Blue Marble as a stitched mosaic, supporting the skeptic's point that it is a constructed composite rather than a single photograph.

title: Why Is Our Skyline Visible From Across the Lake? - Chicago Magazine
snippet: Chicago Magazine piece on seeing the skyline across Lake Michigan via looming.
quote: Turns out I wasn't — not directly, anyway. I was looking at the result of an optical phenomenon called atmospheric refraction, or 'looming,' which is 'the appearance of distant objects that are usually hidden by the convexity of the earth\u2019s surface,' according to Andrew Young, a professor of astronomy at San Diego State University.
stance_why: Mainstream source concedes the long-distance sighting is real while invoking a post-hoc refraction mechanism, supporting the skeptic's anomaly-absorption pattern.

title: Long distance observations - Wikipedia
snippet: Wikipedia survey of long-distance observation records.
quote: The longest distance observation ever has been made on December 15, 2024, from a subpeak near Karag\u00f6l summit, Turkey, toward Shkhara on the Georgia\u2013Russia border at a distance of 493 km. It was photographed by Richard Jezik.
stance_why: Documents a photographed 493 km line of sight, supporting the skeptic's point that extreme long-distance observations are routine and routinely patched by refraction.

title: In 1950, the U.S. Released a Bioweapon in San Francisco - Smithsonian Magazine
snippet: Smithsonian account of the 1950 Operation Sea-Spray bioweapon test.
quote: Beginning on September 26, 1950, the crew of a U.S. Navy minesweeper ship spent six days spraying Serratia marcescens into the air about two miles off the northern California coast. The project was called "Operation Sea Spray."
stance_why: Documents a secret large-scale open-air dispersal over a populated US city, supporting the claim's form as historically precedented.

title: Weather as a Force Multiplier: Owning the Weather in 2025. | National Technical Reports Library - NTIS
snippet: 1996 Air War College paper on military weather modification (NTIS ADA333462).
quote: The purpose of this paper is to outline a strategy for the use of a future weather modification system to achieve military objectives rather than to provide a detailed technical road map.
stance_why: US military paper stating institutional intent to develop weather-modification capabilities, supporting the skeptic's intent leg.

title: Study of Incidence of Hyoid Bone Fractures in Cases of Death due to Hanging, Strangulation and Throttling | Medico-Legal Update | IndianJournals.com
snippet: 2015 forensic study of hyoid fracture incidence across 113 asphyxial deaths.
quote: Incidence of hyoid bone fracture was 2.8% in hanging, 25% in strangulation by ligature and 50% in throttling.
stance_why: Peer-reviewed base rates make Epstein's hyoid fracture ~9x more typical of strangulation than hanging, supporting the homicide reading of the injuries.

title: Trump Admin's Epstein Prison Video Was Likely Modified Using Adobe Premiere Pro: Report - Tech Times
snippet: Tech Times report on WIRED's metadata analysis of the DOJ's Epstein footage.
quote: If a lawyer brought me this file and asked if it was suitable for court, I'd say no. Go back to the source. Do it right,
stance_why: Digital-forensics expert Hany Farid deems the DOJ's 'raw' footage unsuitable for court, supporting the corrupted-record leg.

title: Jeffrey Epstein's Prison Guards Are Indicted On Federal Charges | KNKX Public Radio
snippet: NPR/KNKX report on the federal indictment of Epstein's prison guards.
quote: Two correctional officers who were assigned to guard Jeffrey Epstein on the night he died in his cell have been indicted for allegedly ignoring more than 75 mandatory checks on the wealthy financier then fabricating records to cover it up.
stance_why: Federal indictment for 75+ falsified checks documents the destroyed-evidence asymmetry the skeptic pressed.

title: Apollo 11 missing tapes - Wikipedia
snippet: Wikipedia account of the lost Apollo 11 SSTV telemetry tapes.
quote: The researchers concluded that the tapes containing the raw unprocessed Apollo 11 SSTV signal were erased and reused by NASA in the early 1980s, following standard procedure at the time.
stance_why: Documents the permanent destruction of the raw primary record, supporting the skeptic's chain-of-custody ceiling argument.

title: Moon Rock Turns Out to be Fake - Phys.org
snippet: 2009 Phys.org report on the Rijksmuseum's fake moon rock.
quote: The Dutch national Rijksmuseum made an embarrassing announcement last week that one of its most loved possessions, a moon rock, is a fake -- just an old piece of petrified wood that's never been anywhere near the moon.
stance_why: Documents the Apollo apparatus passing off a fake lunar artifact, supporting the skeptic's point that the program's machinery is not above fabrication.

title: Navy Officially Releases Controversial UFO Videos - The War Zone
snippet: The War Zone on the Pentagon's 2020 release of the Navy UAP videos.
quote: The aerial phenomena observed in the videos remain characterized as "unidentified."
stance_why: Pentagon statement confirming DoD-authenticated videos remain unidentified, supporting the skeptic's authenticated-data leg.

title: Dr. Jon Kosloski: AARO Media Roundtable on FY24 UAP Report - Unidentified Phenomena
snippet: Writeup of AARO director Kosloski's Nov 2024 media roundtable (links defense.gov).
quote: Dr. Kosloski highlighted that less than 3.5% of all cases exhibit truly anomalous characteristics, which could suggest advanced or breakthrough technology.
stance_why: AARO director's own 'truly anomalous' figure supports the skeptic's point that an official investigating office admits cases it cannot explain. Source is an enthusiast-site writeup of the roundtable, not a primary DoD release.
